SMTO-SKL-0162 — The GitHub repository isn't the one SMTO expected

GUID: aaaea879-de06-5d84-bfc6-0cd97d5f91dc
Slug: github-repository-changed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub returned a different repository than the one this request was set up for. It may have been renamed, moved or replaced. SMTO stopped before making any change.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the repository on github.com and check its current owner and name. Note whether it was renamed or moved to another owner. SMTO stops when a repository's identity changes, so you can confirm it's still the one you mean.
  2. Ask SMTO to look up the repository again using its current owner/name. Your request was built on the repository's earlier identity, and a fresh lookup picks up the current one.
  3. If it moved or was renamed, open your GitHub account entry in Parameter Store, update the repository in the authorized repositories list, and select Save. Then repeat your request. SMTO only uses repositories on that list, and the old name no longer matches.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the repository with the owner and name you expect, and your request completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't point the request at a different repository just to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub returned a repository whose numeric ID or full_name differs from the requested/expected identity, or a notification thread belongs to a different repository.

What this means

  • Provider repository ID/full_name differs from expected identity, or a notification thread belongs to another repository. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Provider repository ID/full_name differs from expected identity, or a notification thread belongs to another repository.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare repository_id, owner/name and notification repository identity.

How to fix it

  • GitHubService.execute compares the GET repository endpoint for owner/repo id and full_name with the resolved owner/repo and any supplied repository_id; notification_thread compares the thread's repository.id. Call github.repo again, reconfirm repository_id, owner and name, and update references and authorized_repositories deliberately; renames, transfers and redirects never retarget a request silently.
  • Read github.repo again and reconfirm its exact repository_id, owner and name. Redirects and transfers do not silently change the target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended repository is reconfirmed without following a transfer or redirect silently.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
